DeepWalk does not use Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) or Upper Confidence Bound for Trees (UCT) rollouts, and it does not select random walk paths by an AlphaGo-style tree search. DeepWalk is a graph representation learning method that generates truncated random walks from each node, treats those walks as sentences, and trains a Skip-gram-style objective to learn node embeddings.

Because the premise is false, there is no DeepWalk UCT rollout formula to detail. If one were to invent a hypothetical MCTS-based variant of DeepWalk, a plausible UCT selection rule would be of the standard form

UCT(v) = Q(v) + c * sqrt(ln N(parent(v)) / N(v))

where Q(v) is the estimated value of choosing child node v, N(parent(v)) is the visit count of the parent, N(v) is the visit count of v, and c is an exploration constant. However, this formula is not part of DeepWalk.

In the actual DeepWalk algorithm, the key components are: (1) uniform random walks or truncated random walks sampled from the graph, (2) a corpus of node sequences, and (3) optimization of a Skip-gram objective, typically with hierarchical softmax or negative sampling in related implementations. DeepWalk is commonly evaluated on tasks such as node classification and link prediction.

So the correct answer is that DeepWalk has no UCT rollout formula; the UCT expression above is only a hypothetical MCTS analogue, not a DeepWalk equation.
